facts.statement: Suevoleviathan was an extinct genus of primitive ichthyosaur discovered in the Early Jurassic of Holzmaden, Germany.
facts.quote: Suevoleviathan is an extinct genus of primitive ichthyosaur found in the Early Jurassic (Toarcian) of Holzmaden, Germany.

facts.statement: Suevoleviathan was a large ichthyosaur measuring approximately 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: Suevoleviathan was a large ichthyosaur about 4 m long.

facts.statement: Suevoleviathan was unique among ichthyosaurs for retaining relatively large forefins, unlike others that showed a trend toward smaller forefins.
facts.quote: Suevoleviathan was unique among ichthyosaurs in that it retained relatively large forefins.

facts.statement: The genus Suevoleviathan was named in 1998 by Michael Maisch based on fossils found in the Toarcian-age Posidonia Shale of Holzmaden.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 1998 by Michael Maisch for Leptopterygius disinteger and Ichthyosaurus integer, both found in the Toarcian-age Posidonia Shale of Holzmaden.

facts.statement: The generic name Suevoleviathan means "Swabian Leviathan".
Maisch treated S. integer as a valid species but considered it a metaspecies because its holotype was incomplete and lacked important characters for specific assignment.
facts.quote: While he resultingly treated S. integer as a valid, he nevertheless considered it a metaspecies due to the incompleteness of its holotype, which does not preserve important characters for specific assignment.

facts.statement: Suevoleviathan lived during the Toarcian stage, between 184.2 and 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 174.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: In 2020, Maisch disagreed with the idea that the two species were the same, noting that a reassessed specimen differed from S. disinteger in multiple features, especially in the postcranial skeleton.
rejected.quote: However, in 2020, Maisch disagreed after reassessing a specimen he tentatively assigned to S. integer. This specimen differed from S. disinteger in multiple features, especially in the postcranial skeleton.

rejected.statement: The large forefin of Suevoleviathan suggests it retained a primitive function in low-speed propulsion, while axial undulations of the tail were likely the main method of movement at high speeds.
rejected.quote: The large forefin of Suevoleviathan suggests it retained its plesiomorphic function in low velocity propulsion, although axial undulations of the caudal region were likely still the predominant locomotory mechanism at high velocities.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'The large forefin of Suevoleviathan suggests it retained'

rejected.statement: Maxwell (2018) concluded that the two Suevoleviathan species were growth stages of the same species, a view that Maisch later disputed in 2020.
rejected.quote: Maxwell (2018) concluded that the two Suevoleviathan species are growth stages of the same species, meaning that S. integer has priority and becomes the epithet of the Suevoleviathan type species.
